comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: 2026-10-13: fixed in code, not tried in the real app (the installed Muster could not be replaced that night). Cause: the window sent Shift+Tab with text "\t" and shift marked consumed, so libghostty's kitty encoder (Claude Code's mode) dropped the shift and wrote a plain Tab; a plain shell (legacy mode) was unaffected. Commits 5095f784 (pane send --key shift+tab, bytes pinned by a test) and c21d7b3e (no text for a single control character, as Ghostty's keyAction does; Shift+Return now also keeps its shift in kitty mode). To check by hand after upgrading to 0.16.0: Shift+Tab cycles Claude Code's permission mode in a pane; 'printf "\e[>1u"; cat -v' then Shift+Tab shows ^[[9;2u. Move to done once seen.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
GitHub issue #2 part 3: Shift+Tab does nothing in a Claude Code pane in Muster.app 0.15.0, local or on a remote daemon. In Ghostty the same key cycles Claude Code's permission modes. `~/.muster/config.toml` binds nothing to shift+tab, so Muster either swallows the key or encodes it differently (expected `CSI Z`, or the kitty-keyboard form when the program asks for it).

Not yet checked: what a plain shell sees (`cat -v` in a pane), and whether it worked before 0.15.0. Start there; it splits "the app eats the key" from "the app encodes it wrong". Check the app's key equivalents too, since a menu item or the tab-cycling shortcuts could claim it before the surface does.

Separately, `pane send --key` has no way to press shift+tab, so an agent cannot cycle another agent's permission mode either. Add it alongside the fix.
title: Shift+Tab never reaches Claude Code in a pane
